messages:
sam: Heads-up — Northbridge POC: they're hitting slow TTFT (~700-900ms) on short prompts and occasional 429s under burst concurrency. Sales asking for a triage and asap mitigation so the demo isn't blocked.

anya: Copy. Can you drop reproducible request details and any error logs? I'll pull in eng. :eyes:  @kevin @linda

sam: Minimal repro: 8 concurrent short chat requests (<=30 tokens), model pinned to redwood-l2-quant, payload small. Observed responses: first token latency high, then steady. Also see intermittent 429s when concurrency spikes to 20. Logs: 
```
2025-09-15T14:03:12Z WARN request=abc123 status=200 latency_ms=820 model=redwood-l2-quant kv_cache_hit=false
2025-09-15T14:03:13Z ERROR request=def456 status=429 error=rate_limit_exceeded pool=shared-inference
2025-09-15T14:03:14Z INFO request=ghi789 latency_ms=95 kv_cache_hit=true
```

linda: Thanks. Two quick things we usually check: (1) batching policy on the Dedicated/dev pool (max_batch_size + batch_timeout_ms) and (2) prefix/KV cache config — short prompts benefit a lot from prefix cache.

kevin: On the runtime side — quantized L2 on short sequences sometimes pays a cold-start penalty for first token because kernels pick a slower path when seq_len small. Also if prefix cache isn't warmed you'll see those high first-token latencies. The 429s suggest the shared pool throttling; what's their route config?

sam: Route is `northbridge-demo` -> tiered routing: hosted primary, fallback to shared-dedicated; concurrency limit set to 16 by default.

anya: Can we try an immediate mitigations checklist? 1) Lower `batch_timeout_ms` to 10-20ms to avoid waiting for big batches for short prompts. 2) Reduce `max_batch_size` for this route to 4 so jitter doesn't add. 3) Enable prefix cache and pre-warm with representative prompts. 4) Pin to a low-latency variant (non-quant) for demo if they accept cost delta.

kevin: Agreed. Quick commands (config snippets):
```
# route config
"northbridge-demo": {
  "max_batch_size": 4,
  "batch_timeout_ms": 15,
  "concurrency_limit": 24,
  "model_pin": "redwood-l2-lowlatency"
}
# enable prefix cache
"prefix_cache": {"enabled": true, "warm_prompts": ["/samples/demo-warm.txt"]}
```

linda: For the 429s, suggest bumping route concurrency_limit temporarily and add a fallback policy: `queue` with short ttl so we don't surface rate errors to demo users. Also confirm they aren't hitting org-wide rate quotas — sales, can you share approximate request QPS during demo?

sam: They peak at ~35 requests/sec during scripted load. We can ask them to stagger by 100ms but prefer infra-side fix.

infra-bot: Automated alert: pool=shared-inference cpu_util=78% gpu_util=62% queue_depth=3 recent_errors=12 rate_limited=7

kevin: With 35 QPS and small payloads, prefix cache + lower batch timeout usually drops median TTFT below 250ms and eliminates most 429s if concurrency_limit is raised to ~40 for demo. If we don't want to change model, pre-warming cache is highest ROI.

anya: I'll coordinate with Northbridge SE to pre-warm prompts before the next demo window and propose the temporary config changes. Linda — can you provide a one-paragraph cost delta if we recommend pinning to non-quant (approx. 2.2x token cost) so sales can set expectations?

linda: Yep. I'll draft: "Pinning to redwood-l2-lowlatency increases per-token compute by ~2.2x on our hosted tiers; for a 15-minute demo with 2k tokens total that's ~ $X additional. For Dedicated, small delta if already reserved capacity." I'll send numbers in DM.

sam: Great. Action items: @kevin to push temp route changes and run a quick warm; @anya to coordinate pre-warm with customer and validate demo window; @linda to send cost delta; I'll update Northbridge.

kevin: I'll push changes to the staging route in 10m and post before/after latency numbers here.

anya: Thanks team. Keeping this thread pinned for the POC. :thumbsup:
